title: Finite-family Fourier estimator accuracy
statement: Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign cube $\\{−1,1\\}^n$, let $\\mathcal H$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$, and let $0<\\varepsilon\\le 1/2$. For each $S\\in\\mathcal H$, take the prescribed number of sample inputs, and form the Fourier estimator whose coefficient at $S$ is the empirical average of $f(x)\\prod_{i\\in S}x_i$. If the Fourier weight of $f$ outside $\\mathcal H$ is at most $\\varepsilon/2$, and every estimated coefficient differs from its true Fourier coefficient by strictly less than $\\varepsilon/(2|\\mathcal H|)$, then the Boolean function obtained by taking the sign of the estimated Fourier sum has relative Hamming distance at most $\\varepsilon$ from $f$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the sign cube
$\\mathcal H$ is a nonempty finite family of coordinate subsets
the Fourier weight outside $\\mathcal H$ is at most $\\varepsilon/2$
every empirical coefficient error is strictly less than $\\varepsilon/(2|\\mathcal H|)$
the sample inputs are indexed by each member of $\\mathcal H$ and by the prescribed sample count
